mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates economic weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 70% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 70% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 0.5% QoQ and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances.
